issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+17 Table 3/body assign photometric 81.29 min to WD spin and RV 83.599 min to orbit, while its abstract reverses the method labels; Babina+24 refines spin to 0.05645351(14) d and observes beat 2.0425(145) d; Bruch+25 TESS LC#1/2 report 4877.50(13)/4877.407(91) s with unstated confidence convention; Bernardini+13 reports X-ray 6100±120 and 4960±80 s, and the latter printed hour conversion is arithmetically inconsistent. No paper establishes Pdot/synchronization rate.
issues.why_it_matters: Clock misassignment propagates into spin/orbit/beat comparisons and any synchronization-evolution claim.
issues.needed_action: Please choose the display convention for canonical spin/orbit values and whether the X-ray candidates remain unassigned. Keep all measurements separate until then; verify Bruch uncertainty convention from publisher copy if possible.

issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+17 infer ~16 MG only if an ~8000 Å continuum turnover is the 8th cyclotron harmonic; they say it could be 35% lower and B>~20 MG is very unlikely. No Zeeman or individual harmonics were detected; Bernardini+13 only reports an IR excess/cyclotron contribution.
issues.why_it_matters: Using 16 MG as a direct mean/polar photospheric field would miscompare physical field components across CV populations.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether RAWDOG should expose the conditional ~16 MG estimate and qualitative <~20 MG discussion in separate fields or keep the numeric estimate only in the measurement ledger.

issues.competing_evidence: Bernardini+13 Sect. 3.3/Table 5 gives 0.77 +0.02/-0.03 Msun from a Suleimanov post-shock spectral model; Tovmassian+17 adopts 0.75 Msun as a Doppler-map input. No dynamical WD mass was found.
issues.why_it_matters: Mass-distribution comparisons can mix model-dependent X-ray masses with dynamical masses or adopted map inputs.
issues.needed_action: Decide which population tables may include the X-ray model estimate; retain the 0.75 Msun map input as assumed only. Verify whether Bernardini explicitly defines the mass interval confidence level outside Table 5.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 original VLA Table 1 gives 79±5 μJy; Ridder+23 Table 3 repeats 79±8 μJy with an asterisk because the catalog imposes a minimum 10% error. Same detection, not an independent observation.
issues.why_it_matters: The uncertainty convention affects radio significance and comparisons of flux errors.
issues.needed_action: Choose which uncertainty is shown in the main compatibility catalog; keep both provenance rows and do not average.
